mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized at -20% over four consecutive weeks, indicating a floor in mobility loss. Absent further deterioration, mean-reversion pressure will drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks as pent-up demand and adaptation to restrictions normalize activity levels.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined from -22.0 to -20.0 over four weeks, showing stabilization
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains at or below -20.0, or declines further to -22.0 or lower.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains elevated at +45% despite restrictions, signaling sustained outdoor preference. This behavioral shift will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as consumers substitute indoor retail with outdoor recreation, keeping retail footfall depressed.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above +40 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at +45.0 in t-0w, sustained above +44 for four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls below +30 while RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -15, indicating substitution effect has reversed.

candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -35 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -37.1 in t-0w, stable at -37 to -38 for four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -30 within two weeks and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -18 in the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and RETAIL_REC move in tandem: workplace mobility at -22.1% constrains daytime retail activity. A joint recovery mechanism operates where workplace reopening drives commuter retail spending. Over four weeks, if WORKPLACES rises above -15, RETAIL_REC will rise above -15 due to correlated return-to-work and retail resumption.

evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and RETAIL_REC both declined -22 to -23 range over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -15 but RETAIL_REC remains below -18 in the following four weeks, indicating decoupling of workplace and retail recovery.
